subject: Multi-season occupancy models with sites surveyed in only one season

messages.author: dcdbddc280b1269e
messages.subject: Multi-season occupancy models with sites surveyed in only one season
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am fitting single-species, multi-season occupancy models using data from two fishing cat camera-trap surveys conducted in 2025 and 2026. In 2025, we surveyed 52 sites, whereas in 2026, we resurveyed only 34 of these sites. We used the same survey methodology in both years and collected the same types of covariates, although some vary between years.

I am trying to determine the best way to proceed and would appreciate your advice. So far, I have considered two options:

  • Fit the models using only the 34 sites surveyed in both years. However, this would exclude several sites where fishing cats were detected in 2025 and given the species’ low detection rate, every detection is valuable.

  • Include all 52 sites and represent the unsurveyed sites in 2026 with NAs in the detection history. However, spOccupancy does not allow NAs in the occupancy covariates. The vignette suggests imputing missing values so I was thinking that one possibility would be to use the covariate values collected at these sites in 2025 as imputations for 2026.

    My reasoning is that, since the detection histories for these sites in 2026 would consist entirely of NAs, these site-year combinations would not contribute information to the model. But I am not sure whether it's statistically appropriate or could introduce bias.

    It's important to consider that although some environmental covariates vary between years, differences are relatively small for occupancy variables ("habitat type", "waterbody type", and "distance to human activity", which remain fairly stable over this period). The detection covariate "camera placement", by contrast, varies a bit more between years. 

so to summarise: Would imputing the 2025 occupancy covariate values for sites not surveyed in 2026 be a reasonable approach? 

or would it be preferable to restrict the analysis to sites surveyed in both years, despite losing some of the 2025 detections? 

or are there alternative approaches I should consider for handling this unbalanced sampling design?.


Thank you in advance for your help!

messages.author: 0b274a0ee3490d75
messages.subject: Re: Multi-season occupancy models with sites surveyed in only one season
parts:
Hi Giada, 

Thanks for the question. I would recommend including all sites and setting the 2026 unmeasured site covariate values to the 2025 values. When this is done in spOccupancy, the sites without any samples during a given season do not contribute at all to the estimation of the model parameters, and so there is no risk of bias in the estimated occupancy coefficients when you include the 2025 values for the missing 2026 sites (so long as the y values are NA for those sites). The only place where those covariate values come into place is when calculating the "psi.samples" (occupancy probability) and "z.samples" (latent occupancy) outputs. The function will provide estimates of occupancy for the 2026 sites that weren't sampled using the imputed 2025 covariate values. So, if you do any summarization of the "psi.samples" or "z.samples" objects from the model, you need to be aware that any overall averages or summaries will be including occupancy values in 2026 at the missing sites predicted with the 2025 covariate values. If the covariates don't change from 2025 to 2026, then there isn't really any issue, but the more change in the covariates there is, the more biased the "psi.samples" or "z.samples" predicted values could be for those sites in 2026, so if there is the potential for a lot of covariate change and you want to use the "psi.samples" or "z.samples" output, you simply need to ensure that any summaries with "psi.samples" or "z.samples" only use the site/year where the covariate values were sampled. 

Hope that helps, 

Jeff
